root.name: Center Game: von der Lasa Gambit

overview: White offers the d-pawn, developing the bishop to c4 at once to aim at f7 and prepare Nf3 and castling. Black can keep the pawn with ...Nf6 or ...c5 and ...Bb4+; the main line 3...Nf6 4.e5 d5 5.Bb5+ Nc6 6.Nf3 Ne4 7.Nxd4 leads to rapid piece play with Black safe. White gets quick development and a central majority; Black has an extra pawn and good defences.

white_ideas.idea: Lead in development with Bc4, Nf3 and quick castling
Regain the d4 pawn with Nf3 and Nxd4 or c3
Pressure on f7 along the a2-g8 diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...Nf6, ...Bb4+ or ...c5
Strike with ...d5 to blunt the bishop and free the game
Develop quickly and return material if needed to neutralise attack

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White e-pawn advanced and Black d4 pawn extra

character.notes: A forcing gambit with early piece play and tactics, risk for White.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the d4 pawn with 3...c5 or 3...Nf6 4.e5 d5; White regains it only if Black allows.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious: Black has several good ways to hold the pawn.

structure.notes: Open lines and pieces developed quickly.

approach.notes: Rarely used; a rare gambit chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Line-based gambit; not for beginners and it needs known refutations to answer.

sublines_that_differ.name: Scotch Gambit-type transposition
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Bc4 Nf6 4. Nf3 Nxe4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black grabs a second pawn; White needs concrete compensation.

character.reason: Early gambit with tactics and quick development.

gambit.reason: White gives the d-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black has good ways to hold the pawn; compensation is unclear.

structure.reason: Open centre and quick piece play.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose this gambit.

level.reason: A rare gambit; dubious so never Beginner.

plans.reason: Bc4 and quick development aim at f7.
